precepts.text: Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch: talking about Christ. In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.
precepts.point: In that day shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree: that is in the kingdom.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
In the Persian captivity there was Joshua the high priest, of the tribe of Levi, and Zerubbabel the governor, of the tribe of Judah. The Lord speaks to Joshua and his fellows, “for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” The Branch is Christ, and Jeremiah 23 shows it.

“Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” The righteous Branch raised unto David is Christ, the King who will reign and execute justice.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.” That is the same day Zechariah speaks of. The stone laid before Joshua with its seven eyes, and those eyes are the angels. “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day”: that is Christ dying on the cross. And “In that day”, every man shall call his neighbour “under the vine and under the fig tree”: that is in the kingdom, when Israel dwells safely under the Branch.

precepts.why:

In Christianity they scatter them into the Baptist church, the Catholic church, the holiness church, whatever denomination. We are being divided rather than united as the twelve tribes of Israel. Even in the time of Christ there were the Sadducees, the Pharisees, the Stoics, the Epicureans and the Herodians; we were being scattered then, and it's happening today.

Moses said where it would lead: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” Under these wood gods, like Christianity with the old wooden cross, and the many denominations under Islam, our people are scattered everywhere in those false religions, even in Judaism.

Remember, this is about Israelites; it is not so much talking about Esau. “Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away”: driven them away from the truth that they are the Israelites of the twelve tribes. But the Lord says “I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all countries whither I have driven them”.

“for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord”. We are not just in North America. That is why Jeremiah says “from all countries whither I had driven them”: the 12 tribes were scattered to every corner, and the gathering is from all of them.

It behooves us to learn God's laws, commandments, and statutes, because to set up a government you need everything we read at the beginning of class about what a community consists of. God's laws are going to filter everything for us. And we have to learn to think bigger: not a house, not property; the world is ours. precepts.why:
Isaiah says the government shall be upon his shoulder, “upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice.” Jeremiah says the same: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch.” That righteous Branch is Christ.

“and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” See what he is going to do: execute judgment and justice in the earth. The nations don’t want that. So the throne of David in Isaiah 9 is the reign of this King, the Branch raised unto David. The increase of his government is a kingdom of judgment and justice, of law and order, and in his days Judah is saved and Israel dwells safely. That is why we learn God’s laws now: it is the government we are going to live under.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:

So when Isaiah 33:5 says “The Lord is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness”, it is through Christ, the King, the King of kings.

That is our hope amid destruction. When the Lord rises up, the nations are scattered and their spoil is gathered like the gathering of the caterpillar, and the righteous Branch of David reigns over Zion with judgment and justice.
